All requirements cross-checked against actual source and tests. Findings:

- `src/queue.js`: constructor validates `maxAttempts` as positive integer; `enqueue` validates finite priority, dedupes supplied keys (returns existing job even when completed; `null`/undefined key never dedupes); `dequeue` scans in enqueue order with strict `>` comparison, which correctly yields highest-priority-first with FIFO ties, marks running, increments attempts, returns null when empty; `complete`/`fail` throw on unknown IDs and non-running transitions; `fail` requeues while `attempts < maxAttempts` then marks failed; all returned objects are deep `structuredClone` copies (nested payload/result included); `snapshot()` deep-copies; `restore` validates version/maxAttempts/jobs array, per-job required fields, id/priority/key/status/attempts types, duplicate IDs and duplicate keys, preserves order/results/options, converts `running`→`pending` keeping attempts, and derives next ID (backed by a `#ids` collision-avoiding `#newId`).
- `src/store.js`: `saveQueue` creates parent dirs recursively, writes a same-directory temp file, atomic `rename`, cleanup on rename failure; `loadQueue` returns a fresh queue on ENOENT, propagates `SyntaxError` on malformed JSON and `TypeError` from restore validation.
- `src/cli.js`: `add <JSON-payload> [priority]`, `list`, `next`; persists after add and after a successful dequeue; `die()` writes to stderr and exits 1 for missing args, unknown commands, invalid JSON, invalid priority. The `next` no-save-when-null case is not a mutation, consistent with "persist all mutations".
- `package.json` has `"type": "module"` and `npm test` → `node --test`; README documents library, persistence, CLI, recovery semantics; REQUIREMENTS.md unchanged (matches packet size 2639).
- Tests target the required behaviors (39 node:test cases: dedupe-even-completed, FIFO/priority, attempt-limited fail, encapsulation via mutation probes, restore validation including `payload: undefined`, temp-file cleanup, CLI subprocess exit codes/stderr). Final `npm test` evidence (call_a2b7aec8…) is post-mutation with exit code 0 — node:test exits nonzero on any failure (demonstrated by the earlier failing run exiting 1), so exit 0 establishes pass; an independent CLI smoke test in /tmp also confirmed cross-process persistence and `bad-json-exit=1` with stderr.

Minor non-blocking observations: CLI accepts an empty-string priority argument (`Number('') === 0`, still a finite number so within spec); objects containing `undefined` nested values silently serialize via the JSON round-trip rather than throwing — both deterministic and JSON-safe, no requirement violated.
